transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I suppose it’s the tension, mostly. My neck and shoulders… and my jaw, too. They’re tight almost all the time now, like I’m bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV.
Is the tension in your neck, shoulders, and jaw always present, or does it come and go?
It’s… most of the time, honestly. It eases a bit here and there, but my neck and shoulders and jaw feel tight almost constantly, even when I’m just sitting or trying to watch TV.
Is the tension in your neck, shoulders, and jaw painful?
Yes… it can be painful. Mostly it’s this tight, aching feeling, like I’m bracing myself all the time. My neck and shoulders especially, and sometimes my jaw. It’s pretty constant.
Did something specific happen that you think might have triggered this tension in your neck, shoulders, and jaw?
I think it started after a pipe burst at home. The remodeling afterward turned the place upside down, and… it’s been about seven months since then.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping since the pipe burst and the remodeling at your home?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really kept track. Sleep’s been… different, I guess, but I don’t know if it’s directly because of all that.
Do you often feel tired?
Yeah… pretty often. By the end of the school day I feel really wrung out, and even small things like grading a few quizzes can feel like I’m pushing through mud. Rest doesn’t always seem to reset it.
Do you feel tired even after getting a full night's rest?
Yeah. Even if I’ve slept enough, by the last bell I’m still pretty wrung out. A quiet Sunday doesn’t always fix it either. It’s like even a small stack of quizzes feels harder than it should.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since the pipe burst at your home?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say sad most of the time. It’s been stressful, sure, but I haven’t really thought of it as feeling down exactly.
Do you find yourself feeling less interested in activities that you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure… I don’t think so, not in any clear way. I guess I haven’t really paid much attention to it.
Do you feel tired most days?
Most days, yeah. By the last bell I’m usually pretty wrung out… even if I slept alright. Little things, like grading a few quizzes, can feel heavier than they should.
Have you been feeling irritable most of the time since the pipe burst at your home?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve probably been a bit short at times, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed it most of the time.
Do you feel tired even after engaging in activities that you normally find enjoyable?
Yeah… I suppose so. Even if I’ve done something quiet or nice, it doesn’t really restore me. By the last bell I feel wrung out, and then even a small pile of quizzes feels like… pushing through mud.
Do you have any other areas of your body where you experience pain or discomfort?
Mostly my neck and shoulders. My jaw too, actually. They’re tight a lot of the time… like I’m bracing myself, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV.
Have you had to cut back on your activities because of your symptoms?

Yes… I’ve had to cut back some. I’m behind on lesson prep and grading, more than I’d like to admit. And I stopped doing some of the community-theater organizing I usually handle. I just couldn’t keep up with all of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family since you started experiencing these symptoms?

A bit, I guess. I’ve been less available… mostly because I’m falling behind with lesson prep and grading, and I gave up some of the community-theater work I usually manage. I just couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore.
Do you feel that fatigue is the main symptom that's been bothering you the most?

Yes… I think so. By the end of the school day, when the last bell rings, I just feel wrung out. And it doesn’t really go away with a decent night’s sleep or a quiet Sunday. Even a small stack of quizzes can feel like… pushing through mud.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things in a way that feels hard to control?

Yes… it does feel hard to control sometimes. I’ll tell myself to just focus on the class in front of me, but then one small thing—like a late invoice, or a student falling behind—starts this whole string of what-ifs, and I can’t seem to shut it off.
Do you find yourself worrying about things almost every day?

Yes… most days, I’d say. It jumps around—stuff with the house, whether the contractors missed something, then school… lesson plans, robotics club falling behind. And then I start thinking I’m letting my wife or family down by not keeping it all under control.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

Yes… even when nothing’s actually happening, my mind still kind of goes looking for something. It jumps from the house—like, did the contractors miss something—to school, lesson plans, the robotics kids falling behind… and then whether I’m letting my wife and family down by not keeping it all together.
Do you find yourself having repetitive, intrusive thoughts that you can't get out of your head?

Yes… I suppose so. It’s not like one strange thought exactly, more like I tell myself to stop and pay attention to the class, and then something small—an invoice being late, or a student falling behind—starts this whole run of “what ifs.” And I can’t really switch it off.
